mainPoints.explanation: Delivery Hero achieved 97% data quality (vs GA's 85%), 3x cost savings, and 10x load increase by optimizing their pipeline and eliminating third-party limitations.
mainPoints.point: Building an in-house user tracking service can outperform third-party solutions in data quality, cost, and control.

oneSentenceSummary: This article shares Delivery Hero's journey of replacing Google Analytics with an internal user tracking service, achieving higher data quality (97% vs 85%), 3x cost savings, and 10x load increase through careful architecture, testing, and incremental optimization.
originalTitle: Challenging Google Analytics: Building a Scalable， Cost-Effective User Tracking Service
summary: The article presents a detailed talk by Alina Krasavina, an engineering manager at Delivery Hero, on building and scaling an internal user tracking service (Perseus) to replace Google Analytics. It covers the motivations: migration necessity, real-time data needs, GDPR compliance, and cost control. The initial MVP used a simple API with Pub/Sub processors, which proved highly scalable. The rollout involved parallel testing with a double pipeline (sending data to both GA and internal service), progressive rollout across brands, and load testing with 3x peak traffic. After rollout, data quality improved from 85% to 97% (measured by order match rate), and cost dropped to 25% less than GA, later to 3x cheaper. Post-MVP challenges included data completeness (null standardization), backend reliability (pod restart data loss solved by synchronous requests and retries), and further cost optimizations (data archiving, JSON storage, cheaper nodes). SDK improvements like event prioritization, non-blocking queuing, and monitoring helped prevent data loss during A/B tests. A key innovation was code-generated event models that enforce data quality at compile time, reducing governance overhead. The talk emphasizes the value of a simplistic initial architecture, careful KPI selection, thorough testing, and incremental improvements.
title: Challenging Google Analytics: Building a Scalable， Cost-Effective User Tracking Service
